# CPA final design handoff

Open `CPA_Final_Design.html` in your browser. It contains all 17 views in one file; no web server or installation is required. Use the sidebar, or the Page selector on a narrow screen.

Give your implementation AI both `CPA_Final_Design.html` and `CPA_Implementation_Brief.md`. The HTML is the visual and interaction reference. The brief defines the implementation scope, engineering semantics, page requirements and finite final acceptance checks.

`approved-sources/` preserves the ten individually locked view fragments. `completed-sources/` contains the seven supporting views completed in the final scope. They are source references, not separate runnable applications. The combined file adds navigation adapters to packaged copies while preserving the locked source snapshots.

Use LIC10501 for the approved oscillation investigation example and FIC30502 for the more detailed supplied replay/calculation/configuration records. Unsupported fixture combinations stay explicitly unavailable; the prototype never substitutes another loop's data silently. The production implementation must use the complete real datasets and services.

This is a UI design reference. Signal traces and some examples are illustrative; writes, execution, cryptographic verification and production downloads are not performed. Browser-local notes and draft forms are demonstration behavior only.

`CPA_Validation_Report.json` records local prototype checks. `CPA_Design_Manifest.json` records the view inventory and source hashes. The PNG provides a static preview only.
